env: > PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew), Bun 1.4.4, Apple M4 Max, October 2026. Median µs per operation over 250 rounds, after 125 warmup rounds, interleaved and rotated. Every median is ±3.0% or tighter at 95% confidence.
headline:
Totals only span 1.9x, because every entry pays the same database cost. What the ORM itself adds spans 5x: 291µs for UQL (bunSql), 1550µs for MikroORM.

Each entry is measured against its own driver's floor, so a faster driver is never counted as the ORM's win. Running the same UQL code on Bun SQL instead of `pg` saves 148µs, but only 96µs of that is UQL: the other 52µs is the gap between the two floors, free to anything on that driver.

memory-env: > PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew), Node 24.20.0, Apple M4 Max, October 2026. Median KB allocated per step over 60 rounds after 60 warmup of a 7-step lifecycle. Rounds a garbage collection ran in are discarded, never corrected, and no entry lost more than 1% of its own (MikroORM).
memory-note:
Above the floor the field spans 30.1x: 122KB for UQL, 3676KB for MikroORM, and nested opens it widest: MikroORM's 2089KB against UQL's 87KB.

Almost none of it survives: another 60 lifecycles, collected either side, leave at most 15KB behind (Sequelize), identity maps included. What the table prices is collector pressure, not a resident set that grows.

runtime-env: > Bun 1.4.4, Node 24.20.0, all running the same bundled JavaScript, one at a time against the same database. PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew), Apple M4 Max, October 2026. µs for a whole lifecycle, nearest-rank percentiles over 2000 rounds after 250 warmup, so a p99 is drawn from the 21 slowest rounds.
runtime-note: On `raw pg`, where the code is identical, the runtimes are 24µs apart at p50 but 6268µs apart at p99: Bun leads both, and each p99 is 113% on Bun, 616% on Node above its own p50. Switching runtime moves any single entry by at most 1130µs at p50 (MikroORM), where switching ORM on one runtime moves it 1139-2220µs. Both are differences of measured medians, known to ±40µs and ±35µs, so read them as ranges rather than as a ranking. Ranked by what each ORM adds, every runtime agrees: UQL < Drizzle < TypeORM < Sequelize < Prisma < MikroORM.
